watch_outs: Chicago Permit Requirements: Chicago has extensive permit requirements and inspections for most renovation work Chicago requires permits for almost everything—even decks and fences. The process can be slow, and inspectors are known for strict enforcement. Reddit users recommend using contractors experienced with Chicago DOB processes.

Radon Testing: Illinois has significant radon risk, especially in northern and central regions Illinois recommends radon testing for all homes. Reddit users report many homes exceeding EPA action levels, especially those with basements. Test before finishing a basement and install mitigation if needed.

Basement Flooding & Sump Pumps: Chicago area has significant basement flooding issues, especially with aging infrastructure Combined sewers in Chicago mean heavy rain can cause backups. Reddit users strongly recommend overhead sewers or backflow preventers, plus battery-backup sump pumps. The city offers grants for flood control.

Chicago Bungalow Specifics: The iconic Chicago bungalow has specific renovation considerations Bungalows often have knob-and-tube wiring, small electrical panels, and unique layouts. Reddit users recommend the Historic Chicago Bungalow Association for resources. Adding a second floor (popping the top) has specific permit and structural requirements.

Union vs. Non-Union Labor: Chicago area has strong union presence that affects project costs and contractor selection In Chicago proper, many larger projects use union labor, which is typically higher quality but more expensive. Reddit users note that some suburbs are more flexible. For commercial or multi-unit, union requirements may apply.
